chunks: As for what Saʿd ibn ʿAbd Allah narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from al-Husayn ibn Saʿid, from Faḍālah, from al-ʿAlāʾ ibn Razīn, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, from one of the two of them عليهما السلام, who said:
The muleteer and the camel-driver, when travel presses on them in earnest, then they should shorten.

key_terms.الْجَمَّالُ: a camel-driver or camel-handler engaged in travel work
key_terms.الْمُكَارِي: a muleteer or one who hires out riding animals for transport
key_terms.فَلْيَقْصُرَا: then the two should shorten, meaning shorten the salat (prayer)

ai.seo_question: When should the muleteer and camel-driver shorten their salat (prayer) during travel?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling concerning travelers whose work involves transport, such as the muleteer and the camel-driver. It states that when travel becomes serious and pressing for them, they are to perform shortened prayers.
